angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 185,706,680 km at 225.73 pc = 11 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 92791: distance 225.734 pc, the paper's parallax inverted (Gaia DR1's where it revised the star's, else the Hipparcos reduction of van Leeuwen 2007; section 2.3; fractional uncertainty 0.041), at which the luminosity and radius hold (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433): 225.734 +/- 9.255 pc; Gaia DR3 parallax 4.2352 +/- 0.2951 mas (same row, RUWE 4.77), 14.3 standard errors, is not used
radiusSource: Radius 266.935 solar radii from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 92791: radius 266.935 solar radii, implied by the fitted luminosity 8666.21 solar luminosities (fractional uncertainty 0.084) and temperature (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433): 185,706,680 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. No mass is measured, so GM is 0, the records' unpublished value. Temperature 3411 +/- 125 K from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 92791: effective temperature 3411 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.057) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 92791: effective temperature 3411 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.057) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433)
